stories.headline: US forces hit Iranian sites as military action expands across Middle East
stories.body:
American forces completed air strikes against Iranian military targets across the region, according to US Central Command. The military strikes hit Iranian air-defence sites. They also targeted mine-laying capabilities. In addition, the strikes hit communications facilities. Iran's health minister said recent US strikes on Iran killed 18 people. The minister said 108 people suffered injuries in those strikes.

Iran responded with strikes of its own in the region. Iran's IRNA news agency reported that the IRGC Aerospace Force launched a ballistic missile attack. The missile attack targeted Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan. IRNA reported that the attack destroyed several drones. At the same time, misleading posts appeared online. Old and unrelated videos from Dubai, Russia, and the US circulated on social media. Users falsely claimed the videos showed new Iranian strikes on American bases.

Action in sea lanes also caused alarm. Saudi Arabia condemned an attack on the Saudi-owned supertanker Sidr. The attack happened in the Strait of Hormuz. It killed two Filipino seafarers. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said 17 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz by ship on Monday.

US President Donald Trump spoke about the situation on social media. Trump claimed on Truth Social that the United States has almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz. He suggested on social media that the waterway could be renamed the Trump Strait. Trump also said Iran's economy is totally collapsing. Reports by ABC News said Trump was attempting to force Iran back to negotiations. Trump rejected those news reports.

The conflict brought criticism to the US military leadership. US Senator Thom Tillis called on Trump to fire Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. Tillis said there was a leadership void in the military. Former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation. His resignation came after reported disagreements with Hegseth. American voters showed strong opposition to the military policy. A University of Massachusetts poll was released on August 31. The poll showed that more than two-thirds of Americans disapprove of how the Trump administration handles the war with Iran.

stories.headline: Germany and EU accuse Russia over attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport
stories.body:
German police identified two suspects after finding three explosive-laden drones at Leipzig Airport on August 4, 2026. The suspects include a Belarusian carrying a Russian passport. Police also identified an individual holding both Latvian and Russian passports. Leipzig/Halle Airport serves as the home for NATO's Strategic Airlift International Solution. The program delivers equipment along NATO's eastern flank.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the incident marked a new escalation on European Union soil. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany is not at war, but is a daily target of hybrid warfare. Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Germany's accusations about the attack. Putin alleged that evidence had been planted.

The German government decided to shut down the Russian consulate in Bonn. Germany also decided to close the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas announced new actions. She said the EU is preparing sanctions against an additional 1,600 people and entities linked to Russia's military sector.

stories.headline: Devastating floods in Nepal spark major rescue operations in hydropower tunnels
stories.body:
Rescuers in Nepal searched for survivors after a glacier collapse caused catastrophic flooding. At least 1,204 people are confirmed dead in Nepal. More than 4,200 people remain missing. Families in Nepal held symbolic funerals while search efforts continued. In Betrawati, a local resident waited for his wife's body to be retrieved after floods destroyed his village.

Nepal Electricity Authority board member Amshu Kiran Shahi spoke about trapped workers. He said rescue teams were trying to reach about 900 missing workers inside hydropower project tunnels. Difficult weather and heavy rains worsened rescue operations for the trapped tunnel workers. A 23-member team of Indian rat miners offered to join search and rescue operations in Nepal.

The flooding also affected nearby regions. In Tibet, China raised its flood death toll to 21 people. China listed 541 people as missing in Tibet.

stories.headline: Maltese court acquits businessman Yorgen Fenech in 2017 murder of journalist
stories.body:
A Maltese jury acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating a 2017 car-bomb murder. The jury cleared Fenech on both charges by an 8-1 majority vote after eight hours of deliberation. Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia was killed by a car bomb near her home in Malta on October 16, 2017. Fenech's defense team argued that Keith Schembri was the true mastermind behind the murder. Schembri was the former chief of staff to Prime Minister Joseph Muscat. Muscat stepped down as prime minister in January 2020 due to political fallout from the assassination.

Other people have already been convicted for the murder. Brothers George Degiorgio and Alfred Degiorgio pleaded guilty in 2022 to carrying out the murder. Courts sentenced both brothers to 40 years in prison. In June 2025, Robert Agius and Jamie Vella were convicted of supplying the bomb. A court sentenced Agius and Vella to life in prison.

stories.headline: US oversees major oil investment deals between Venezuela and Chevron
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced an agreement on majority ownership of Venezuelan oil reserves. Trump said the US will take majority ownership of over 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's oil reserves. The deal follows major political changes in Caracas. US special forces captured former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro during a raid on Caracas in January 2026.

Major energy firms signed agreements worth tens of billions of dollars with Venezuela. The companies include Chevron, Italy's ENI, and GE Vernova. Chevron announced plans to invest over $7 billion over the next five years in Venezuela's Orinoco Belt. The investment aims to expand production to about 600,000 barrels per day.

Officials praised the agreements. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright spoke in Caracas. Wright said the agreement is Trump's grand plan to replace conflict with commerce. Interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez called it a win-win deal. Rodríguez said the deal would generate over $209 billion in revenue.

stories.headline: Israel signals plans for Gaza population resettlement amid West Bank violence
stories.body:
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said US President Donald Trump froze a proposal on Gaza. Katz said Trump froze, rather than cancelled, a proposal to remove Palestinians from Gaza. US Senator Chris Van Hollen called for an end to US military aid complicity after the statement. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited a military post in Gaza. Netanyahu said Israel will remain on the yellow line until Hamas is disarmed. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir published a video taking direct credit for harsh living conditions imposed on Palestinian detainees.

Casualties continued to rise in Gaza and the West Bank. The Gaza health ministry said 73,470 people have been killed in Gaza during the war. More than 1,330 people died since an October 2025 ceasefire. The ministry added that over 900 people died in Israeli attacks in Gaza during 2026. In the West Bank, Israeli soldiers and settlers raided the village of al-Mughayyir. The raid killed two 19-year-old Palestinians. OCHA reported that settlers or Israeli forces have killed at least 79 Palestinians in the West Bank since early 2026. The dead included 19 children.

OCHA reported that at least 79 Palestinians, including 19 children, have been killed in the West Bank by settlers or Israeli forces since the start of 2026.

stories.headline: Ayodhya Ram Temple Trust appoints retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as CEO
stories.body:
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust appointed retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as CEO. The Trust appointed Mishra as its first Chief Executive Officer. Trust officials chose Mishra after a long selection process. The team evaluated 5,585 applications for the top administrative post. They shortlisted three final candidates before selecting Mishra. Mishra said he learned about his appointment through television news broadcasts.

Mishra brings decades of military experience to his new administrative role. He served in the Indian Air Force for nearly 39 years before his retirement. Mishra retired from the Indian Air Force on April 30, 2026. During his military career, he commanded the Western Air Command of the Indian Air Force. He led the command during Operation Sindoor. Mishra received the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal for his military service.

The Trust also made several other major leadership changes. It appointed Govind Dev Giri as its new General Secretary. Giri succeeds former General Secretary Champat Rai in the role. The Trust selected Mahesh Bhagchandka as its new treasurer. In addition, three new trustees joined the organization. The Trust inducted Madan Mohan Pandey, Mahesh Bhagchandka, and Dr Nirmala Yadav as new trustees.

The new appointments followed serious allegations against previous temple officials. Former General Secretary Champat Rai resigned from his post on June 26. Trustee Anil Mishra also resigned on the same day. Both men resigned on moral grounds after allegations of donation embezzlement. The resignations followed an investigation into cash handling at the temple. Uttar Pradesh's Special Investigation Team released a preliminary report on June 23. The report found 70 instances of counting staff hiding cash in their clothing and shoes at the Ram temple.

stories.headline: Government and opposition clash over accuracy of India's GDP growth data
stories.body:
Union Minister Piyush Goyal said India's 7.8 percent GDP growth figure is real. Goyal said ministers do not manufacture data. Data released by MoSPI on August 31 showed real GDP grew 7.8 percent in Q1 FY27. MoSPI estimated real GDP at Rs 81.36 lakh crore. Nominal GDP reached Rs 88.27 lakh crore in Q1 FY27. That figure was up 10.3 percent from Rs 80 lakh crore in Q1 FY26. India's former Chief Economic Adviser said the double deflator methodology provides a better approach for calculating GDP.

Opposition leaders and former officials questioned the figures. Former Finance Secretary Subhash Garg made a claim about the revision. He said growth would have been about 2.6 percent if last year's Q1 GDP had not been revised down from roughly Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore. MoSPI said Q1 FY26 GDP was first estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore under the 2011-12 base year. It was revised to Rs 80.32 lakh crore after introducing the 2022-23 base year in February 2026. Sanjeev Sanyal said updating the base year was delayed due to the Covid-19 pandemic. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh called the calculations statistical gymnastics. SBI Group Chief Economic Adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh spoke to NDTV about doubts raised regarding the GDP data.

claims.text: Union Minister Piyush Goyal stated that ministers do not manufacture data and asserted that India's 7.8 percent GDP growth figure is real.
According to MoSPI data released on August 31, India's real GDP grew 7.8 percent in Q1 FY27, with real GDP estimated at Rs 81.36 lakh crore.
India's nominal GDP reached Rs 88.27 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, up 10.3 percent from Rs 80 lakh crore in Q1 FY26.
India's former Chief Economic Adviser stated that the double deflator methodology provides a better approach for calculating GDP.

Former Finance Secretary Subhash Garg claimed that Q1 FY27 GDP growth in current prices would have been about 2.6 percent if last year's Q1 GDP had not been revised down from roughly Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh criticized the GDP calculations as statistical gymnastics, citing a gap between implied GDP inflation of 2.3 percent and wholesale price index inflation exceeding 9 percent.

MoSPI stated that Q1 FY26 GDP was initially estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore under the 2011-12 base year, but was revised to Rs 80.32 lakh crore after introducing the 2022-23 base year series in February 2026.
Sanjeev Sanyal, a member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council, stated that updating the GDP base year to 2022-23 was delayed due to the Covid-19 pandemic.
SBI Group Chief Economic Adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh spoke to NDTV regarding doubts raised about India's GDP growth data.

stories.headline: India strongly condemns demolition of century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan
stories.body:
India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the destruction of a century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan. The destroyed temple was located in Siraj village in Narowal district. It was demolished on August 21 and was estimated to be 100 to 125 years old. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the event a reprehensible act of vandalism. Jaiswal requested Pakistani authorities to conduct a transparent investigation and restore the temple.

Accounts differed on how the temple was destroyed. Minority rights group Pakistan Masiha Millat Party alleged people demolished the temple to expand an adjacent seminary. Its chairman Aslam Parvez Sahotra approached authorities to seek legal action against those responsible. But Pakistan's Evacuee Trust Property Board said the structure collapsed due to heavy rainfall.

stories.headline: Heavy rainfall and severe flooding submerge parts of North India
stories.body:
Authorities in Uttar Pradesh evacuated 16,784 people to safety due to persistent flooding. The evacuations took place across 23 affected districts. Three people died in rain-related incidents in Uttar Pradesh. The victims included an 18-month-old child in Pratapgarh and two men aged 32 and 55 in Amroha. State officials deployed 1,499 boats and 1,067 medical teams to support flood relief.

In Bihar, authorities opened all 69 gates of the Sone Barrage at Indrapuri on Wednesday. The action allowed a water discharge of 5.59 lakh cusecs. Major rivers in Bihar flowed above danger marks at multiple locations. These included the Kosi, Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Ganga, and Punpun rivers.

Nationwide rainfall remained below expected levels. Cumulative rainfall during the southwest monsoon season was 13 percent below normal as of September 2. India received 618.5 mm of rain compared to the normal figure of 714.3 mm.
